chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'two just men among you'
He said: The just one is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Imam after him
Then he said: This is among that which the scribes made a mistake in.
ai.seo_question: Who are the 'two just men' mentioned in Surah Al-Ma'idah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) interprets the Quranic phrase 'two just men among you' as referring specifically to the Messenger of Allah and the succeeding Imam, grounding this in the Shia doctrine of divine appointment. He notes that this reading highlights a potential scribal error ('akhṭa’at bihi al-kuttab') in the written text, suggesting a nuanced distinction between the oral transmission of meaning and the literal written form. This hadith underscores the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in interpreting Quranic verses and illustrates the concept of ta'wil within Shia scholarship.
